reason: The bytes are the declared ones (length, SHA-256) and one of the four allowed formats, the one declared; the header is within the pixel ceiling; libvips, in a sandbox with a time and a memory limit, makes a full and a display WebP with no metadata, within 350 and 150 KiB. READY under the row lock; the upload itself is deleted after the commit. A voice note: its bytes are one of the seven recorder containers, the one declared; ffmpeg, in the same sandbox, reads it through that container's demuxer and allowed decoders only, from a file only; its length is at most 61 s, by its container and by what it transcodes to; it is kept as one Ogg Opus file, mono, 24 kbit/s, with no tags or chapters, at most 500 KiB, under v/{uuid}/voice.ogg, and READY with durationMs. The upload is deleted after the commit.

reason: The bytes are not the declared ones, not an allowed format, not the declared format (a HEIC must list HEVC images only), over the pixel or the decoded-bytes ceiling, unreadable (a truncated file included), too slow or impossible to fit: FAILED, final, and the upload is deleted. A storage that cannot be reached is not a refusal: the outbox retries, and the photo stays PROCESSING; an outage before the decode never counts against it. Once five decodes have begun and none finished, the next delivery fails it (TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS) and succeeds. A voice note fails the same way for the same causes, and also when it is longer than 61 s (by its container, or by what it transcodes to), carries a stream no allowed decoder reads (a picture, another codec), or would be kept over 500 KiB.
